page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under KVM virtualization, the instance provides 32 vCPUs across 16 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. System memory totals 256.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU density ratio. Hardware GPU accelerators are absent, and local disk storage is not bundled, requiring persistent data to reside on external block storage. Network baseline connectivity is rated at 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong per-core computational capabilities, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2018.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3092.38, both residing in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-core performance is solid with a Geekbench multi-core score of 17012.0 and Passmark CPU evaluation reaching 47232.41. The memory subsystem achieved a strong Passmark memory score of 2784.7, supported by large-block read bandwidth of 96.44 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, while vector processing benefits from AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16.

Operational tradeoffs include complete reliance on networked storage for persistent I/O, which dictates storage throughput limits. The high RAM-to-core ratio provides cost efficiency by serving memory-intensive requirements without incurring overhead from unneeded additional CPU cores. Suitable workload fits include in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, data transformation pipelines, and medium-scale enterprise application backends.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, the system delivers an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, aligning with memory-intensive compute requirements. The instance omits bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing network storage and providing 20 Gbps baseline networking throughput. In synthetic benchmarks, it achieves top-quartile single-core metrics alongside strong Passmark memory and cryptographic results, supported by AVX-512 and VAES instruction sets. While multi-core stress testing and database operations place in the median range, the high memory density provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads constrained by RAM rather than core saturation. The instance is structured for in-memory databases, large Redis key-value stores, distributed memory caching, and analytical processing.
